item.title: Michael S Barr: Will artificial intelligence broadly raise living standards or drive income and wealth inequality?
item.speaker: Michael S Barr

rating.summary: Michael Barr's speech at the Federal Reserve's Financial Inclusion Conference focuses on the potential economic and distributional consequences of artificial intelligence. He explores two scenarios: AI broadly raising living standards for lower- and middle-income workers, or AI exacerbating inequality by eliminating jobs and concentrating wealth. The speech draws on historical parallels with past general-purpose technologies like electricity and the internet.
rating.stance_rationale: This speech addresses AI, financial inclusion, and income inequality rather than monetary policy, interest rates, or the Fed's policy stance. No monetary policy content is present.
key_quotes: AI has the potential to transform lives and the U.S. economy, possibly empowering workers to be more productive, with lower- and middle-income workers benefiting the most.
When the benefits are concentrated among relatively few people, technology can widen inequalities of income and wealth, especially during the transition period.
